name: Bicycle
style: low-poly, flat colours; simple diamond-frame street bike with round tubes, no spokes, chain or pedals (Quaternius Public Transport, 2017)

source.author: Quaternius
source.note: Wave 1 row 130 was a gap (no bicycle in any planned source); this fills it from Quaternius's CC0 LowPoly Public Transport pack on OpenGameArt. The pack has two bikes, Bicycle and SquareFrameBicycle: the same diamond frame, wheels, handlebar and saddle, one with round tubes (2812 tris) and one with square-section tubes (1144 tris). Bicycle is used: round tubes shade as clean cel bands and read closer to a steel city bike, the square one looks boxier up close. Neither is a true mamachari (no step-through frame, basket, mudguards or chain guard); it reads as a plain street or school bike. The .blend member is used, not the FBX or OBJ: those carry only grey #e7e7e7 materials, which gltf-transform merges into one, while the .blend keeps the red frame, dark tyres, grips and saddle. Height 1.0 m to the top of the handlebar grips; then it is 1.85 m long (a 26-inch city bike is about 1.8-1.9 m), 0.47 m wide, wheels 0.60 m across. Front wheel toward +Z (yaw 180), both tyres on y = 0. For a rider (metres, model space): saddle top at (0, 0.89, -0.31), the saddle spans z -0.45 to -0.17; handlebar grips at (+-0.19, 0.975, 0.455), each grip spans |x| 0.14-0.24; front hub (0, 0.30, 0.62), rear hub (0, 0.30, -0.62); bottom bracket (crank axle) at about (0, 0.29, -0.34). Pedals and cranks are not modelled: put the feet at about (+-0.12, 0.12-0.46, -0.34 +- 0.17) on a 0.17 m crank circle around the bottom bracket. Static, no clips; wheels are separate nodes (FrontWheel, BackWheel) in the GLB.
